title: Lunar phase gave no clear higher large-event share in matched shallow ComCat groups in 2000-2025
abstract: We tested whether the share of M6.5 or larger events among shallow M5.5 or larger earthquakes rises near new and full moon. We used 10,473 ComCat events in 2000-2025, including 913 large events. We matched location cells, two-year periods and preferred magnitude types. Twice the fitted slope on the cosine of doubled lunar phase was -0.795 percentage points, with a conditional 95% two-year block interval of -2.299 to +0.701 points. A local block phase-rotation test gave a two-sided p-value of 0.404. Global block rotations and all planned checks gave no clear positive evidence. The two time periods had opposite point signs. This extends earlier campaign tide-size work with a matched statistic and a null that keeps local sequences. It is not independent confirmation. Lunar phase is not fault stress or ocean loading. Mixed magnitude scales, boundary effects, 13 time blocks and mutable source data limit inference. Code, aggregate evidence, a figure, source hashes and a separate numerical audit are included. External source records remain outside the publication.

display.caption: Fitted new/full minus quarter large-event share contrasts. Bars show conditional 95% two-year block intervals. Only the primary row is the main test. Lunar phase does not measure local tidal stress.
